newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London shares hit new peak, Frankfurt falls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London shares hit new peak, Frankfurt falls.

text.p: London stocks climbed to record levels for the second day running on Wednesday but Frankfurt floor trading fell after hitting peaks in the previous day's hectic market.

On currency markets the dollar was unchanged with traders warily awaiting the U.S. central bank's "beige book" on business conditions, due at 1800 GMT. Sterling was calm after its exuberant jump in reaction to Tuesday's British interest rate hike.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, leapt 0.5 percent in early trade to 4543.2 points, eclipsing the previous best intra-day peak set on Tuesday. Frankfurt was down 0.4 percent in thin trade but Paris, which performed poorly on Tuesday, perked up to show small gains.
European markets drew some comfort from Wall Street which chalked up its second record close in a row overnight, though the rally was far more subdued than Monday's 143-point gain.
London's strong showing on Wednesday was prompted in part by weak industrial production figures which pointed to low inflationary pressures.

But the pace of the climb was slower than the rapid movement seen on Tuesday amid euphoria over the new Labour government's decision to grant the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates without political interference.
"There was a lot of news yesterday which needs to be digested, said one trader. "What do we do for an encore?".
Besides hitting an intra-day peak on Tuesday, London's blue-chip FTSE Index closed 63.7 points higher to a record close of 4,519.3.

Finance minister Gordon Brown's move to grant the British central bank more independence was well received by the markets, still uncertain about how tough Labour would be on inflation. But some investors may question the likely impact on the equity market of the policy shift.

"Eddie George (Bank of England governor) may be much more willing to put up interest rates," one said. "We may now get another interest rate rise as soon as next month, or a steady trickle of rate rises which the market will grow to hate."

In Frankfurt, the fall in floor trade was seen as consolidation after Tuesday's record close. It was also reflecting yestereday's after-hours computerised deals on the IBIS index which ended down 0.5 percent after an unsteady start on Wall Street.
Trading volumes were thin, the market's mood edgy and activity generally subdued ahead of a national holiday on Thursday.
Paris pre-holiday trade, up 0.4 percent, was buoyed by a "reassuring" message from President Jacques Chirac who waded into the parliamentary election campaign to support the ruling conservatives.
The bourse was also underpinned by Wall Street, although traders said the U.S. influence had taken a back seat to political developments in France.
In currencies, the dollar was virtually unchanged from Tuesday;s levels, shrugging off signs of marked improvement in Japan's trade position.
Traders were waiting for the Beige Book for clues on whether the U.S. central bank, the federal Reserve, would move on interest rates at its next policy meeting on May 20, analysts said.

They said the market was currently more concerned with fundamentals than with trade data but warned that indications of an increasingly healthy Japanese trade position could begin to weigh on the dollar.
Elsewhere, sterling fell after tuesday's excitment , standing at $1.6313 and 2.8114 marks in early trade versus $1.6372 and 2.8185 in late Europe yesterday.
STOCKS PRICES AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 24.0 points at 4,543.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 9.61 points at 2,661.54.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 16.09 points at 3,552.19.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7227 marks compared with 1.7229 marks late in Europe on Monday. It was at 125.20 yen, compared to 126.44 on Tuesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.65 an ounce, compared to Tuesday's close in London of $342.85. Silver was $4.73, down two cents.
